definition_title: Composition of the canonical large-height estimates
definition:

Authors: The iut contributors

Independent adaptation of the high-height composition in
Iut/Implication/Corollary23.lean. The mathematical children are explicit
hypotheses; this file does not import their open theorem declarations.
-/
import Definitions.Def_TripodCanonicalHighHeightInputs
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Lattice
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod

/-- The exact canonical children imply the existing `HighHeightEstimate`.
The finite exceptional set is absorbed into the final `htCan` threshold.
The error coefficient is enlarged with existing `logDiff_nonneg` and
`logCond_nonneg`; no Northcott input is needed for this high-height step. -/
theorem highHeightEstimate_of_canonical_children
    (hCompare : CanonicalLegendreHeightComparison)
    (hC2 : CanonicalCorollary22HighHeightEstimate)
    (hEpsilon : EpsilonELargeHeight) : HighHeightEstimate := by
  intro d hd ε hε K
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := hCompare K
  obtain ⟨E, H₂, C₂, hE, hc2⟩ := hC2 d hd K
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := (hE.image (fun x : Pt => htCan x)).bddAbove
  let T : ℝ := max H₂
    (max (((60 * deltaBound d) ^ 2 * (2 * deltaBound d + 4) / ε) ^ 4) 1)
  refine ⟨max M (T / 6 + B), C₂ + B, ?_⟩
  intro x hxK hxd hxH
  have hCompareX := (abs_le.mp (hB x hxK)).1
  have hTransfer : htCan x ≤ auxiliaryHeight x / 6 + B := by
    linarith
  have hxE : x ∉ E := by
    intro hxE
    have hxM : htCan x ≤ M := hM (Set.mem_image_of_mem _ hxE)
    have hMH : M ≤ max M (T / 6 + B) := le_max_left _ _
    linarith
  have hT : T ≤ auxiliaryHeight x := by
    have hTH : T / 6 + B ≤ max M (T / 6 + B) := le_max_right _ _
    linarith
  have hH₂ : H₂ ≤ auxiliaryHeight x := (le_max_left _ _).trans hT
  have hδ : 1 ≤ deltaBound d := by
    have hdNat : 1 ≤ d := hd
    have hdReal : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hdNat
    unfold deltaBound
    linarith
  have hεE : epsilonE (deltaBound d) (auxiliaryHeight x) ≤ ε := by
    apply hEpsilon (deltaBound d) (auxiliaryHeight x) ε hδ hε
    · exact ((le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans hT
    · exact ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans hT
  obtain ⟨hEstimate, _, _⟩ := hc2 x hxK hxd hxE hH₂
  have hNonneg : 0 ≤ logDiff x + logCond x :=
    add_nonneg (logDiff_nonneg x) (logCond_nonneg x)
  have hCoefficient :
      (1 + epsilonE (deltaBound d) (auxiliaryHeight x)) *
          (logDiff x + logCond x) ≤
        (1 + ε) * (logDiff x + logCond x) :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (add_le_add le_rfl hεE) hNonneg
  linarith

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod
natural_language_statement:
> “But such an inequality follows immediately, in light of the [relevant] equality of BD-classes of Corollary 2.2, (i), from Corollary 2.2, (ii) [cf. condition (C2)], (iii) […]”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV*, §2, proof of Corollary 2.3.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.highHeightEstimate_of_canonical_children`

Let $P=\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$. For $x\in P$, let $F_x=\mathbb Q(x)$, let $n_x$ be the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb Q$ (so $n_x\ge1$), and regard $x$ as the distinguished generator of $F_x$. Put $h_x=\log H_{1,F_x}(x)/n_x$, where $\log H_{1,F_x}$ is the logarithmic height supplied by the number-field height construction; put $D_x=\log|\operatorname{disc}(F_x)|/n_x$ and $R_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\log N\mathfrak p_v$, where the sum runs over the finite places $v$ of $F_x$ satisfying $v(x)\ne1$ or $v(x-1)\ne1$, and $N\mathfrak p_v$ is the absolute ideal norm of the maximal ideal associated with $v$. Set $J_x=256(x^2-x+1)^3/(x^2(x-1)^2)$ and $A_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\max\{\log(v(J_x)),0\}$, with this latter sum over all finite places of $F_x$ and with the convention that a sum over an arbitrary index set is the sum of its nonzero terms if there are finitely many, and is zero otherwise. The denominator defining $J_x$ is nonzero, but $J_x$ can be zero; the real logarithm used here has $\log0=0$, so these summands are then zero. A datum $K=(V,c)$ consists of a finite set $V$ of natural-number primes, a proof that every member is prime, a proof that $2\in V$, and an arbitrary real number $c$. Define $S_K\subseteq P$ by requiring both $|\log(v(x))|\le c$ and $|\log(v(x-1))|\le c$ at every finite place whose residue field has characteristic in $V$, and both $|\log(w(x))|\le c$ and $|\log(w(x-1))|\le c$ at every infinite place $w$ of $F_x$. These expressions use the values assigned by the places in the supplied number-field constructions. There is no sign restriction on $c$, and $S_K$ is allowed to be empty. Write $\Delta_d=552960d$ and $e(\delta,t)=(60\delta)^2\log(2\delta t)/\sqrt t$ using total real logarithm, square root, and division. Assume three hypotheses: first, for every datum $K$ there exists a real $B$ such that $|A_x/6-h_x|\le B$ for every $x\in S_K$; second, for every natural number $d>0$ and every datum $K$ there exist a finite set $E\subseteq P$ and reals $H_2,C_2$ such that every $x\in S_K$ with $n_x\le d$, $x\notin E$, and $H_2\le A_x$ satisfies simultaneously $A_x/6\le(1+e(\Delta_d,A_x))(D_x+R_x)+C_2$, $e(\Delta_d,A_x)\le1$, and $0\le D_x+R_x$; third, for every three real numbers $\delta,t,\eta$, the conditions $1\le\delta$, $0<\eta$, $(((60\delta)^2(2\delta+4))/\eta)^4\le t$, and $1\le t$ imply $e(\delta,t)\le\eta$. Under these three hypotheses, for every natural number $d>0$, every real $\varepsilon>0$, and every datum $K$, there exist real numbers $H,C$ such that every $x\in P$ satisfying $x\in S_K$, $n_x\le d$, and the strict inequality $H<h_x$ satisfies $h_x\le(1+\varepsilon)(D_x+R_x)+C$. None of the existential real constants has an imposed sign restriction. The finite exceptional set in the second hypothesis may be empty and need not be contained in $S_K$ or in the degree range; the conclusion contains no exceptional set. The hypotheses and conclusion make no requirement at $d=0$, and their pointwise requirements are vacuous when the relevant set of qualifying points is empty.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.highHeightEstimate_of_canonical_children`

令 $P=\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$。对任意 $x\in P$，令 $F_x=\mathbb Q(x)$，令 $n_x$ 为 $x$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上的最小多项式的次数，因而 $n_x\ge1$，并将 $x$ 视为 $F_x$ 中的指定生成元。定义 $h_x=\log H_{1,F_x}(x)/n_x$，其中 $\log H_{1,F_x}$ 是数域高度构造给出的对数高度；定义 $D_x=\log|\operatorname{disc}(F_x)|/n_x$，以及 $R_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\log N\mathfrak p_v$，此处求和遍历满足 $v(x)\ne1$ 或 $v(x-1)\ne1$ 的 $F_x$ 的有限位，$N\mathfrak p_v$ 是相应极大理想的绝对理想范数。令 $J_x=256(x^2-x+1)^3/(x^2(x-1)^2)$，并令 $A_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\max\{\log(v(J_x)),0\}$，后一个和遍历 $F_x$ 的所有有限位，并采用如下约定：若非零项只有有限个，则取这些非零项之和，否则取零。$J_x$ 的分母非零，但 $J_x$ 可以为零；所用实对数满足 $\log0=0$，此时后一个和的各项均为零。数据 $K=(V,c)$ 包含自然数素数组成的有限集 $V$、其每个元素都是素数的证明、$2\in V$ 的证明，以及任意实数 $c$。定义 $S_K\subseteq P$：对剩余域特征属于 $V$ 的每个有限位 $v$，均有 $|\log(v(x))|\le c$ 和 $|\log(v(x-1))|\le c$；对 $F_x$ 的每个无限位 $w$，均有 $|\log(w(x))|\le c$ 和 $|\log(w(x-1))|\le c$。这些表达式使用给定数域构造中各个位赋予元素的数值。$c$ 没有符号限制，$S_K$ 可以为空。记 $\Delta_d=552960d$，并记 $e(\delta,t)=(60\delta)^2\log(2\delta t)/\sqrt t$，其中使用全定义的实对数、平方根和除法。 假设以下三个命题。第一，对每个数据 $K$，存在实数 $B$，使每个 $x\in S_K$ 都满足 $|A_x/6-h_x|\le B$。第二，对每个正自然数 $d$ 和每个数据 $K$，存在有限集 $E\subseteq P$ 以及实数 $H_2,C_2$，使每个满足 $n_x\le d$、$x\notin E$ 和 $H_2\le A_x$ 的 $x\in S_K$ 都同时满足 $A_x/6\le(1+e(\Delta_d,A_x))(D_x+R_x)+C_2$、$e(\Delta_d,A_x)\le1$ 和 $0\le D_x+R_x$。第三，对任意三个实数 $\delta,t,\eta$，若 $1\le\delta$、$0<\eta$、$(((60\delta)^2(2\delta+4))/\eta)^4\le t$ 且 $1\le t$，则 $e(\delta,t)\le\eta$。在这三个假设下，对每个正自然数 $d$、每个正实数 $\varepsilon$ 和每个数据 $K$，存在实数 $H,C$，使每个满足 $x\in S_K$、$n_x\le d$ 和严格不等式 $H<h_x$ 的 $x\in P$ 都满足 $h_x\le(1+\varepsilon)(D_x+R_x)+C$。所有存在量化的实常数均没有符号限制。第二个假设中的有限例外集可以为空，也不必包含于 $S_K$ 或相应次数范围内；结论不包含例外集。这些假设及结论对 $d=0$ 不作要求，且当符合条件的点集为空时，相应的逐点要求即为空真。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.highHeightEstimate_of_canonical_children`

$P=\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ とする。各 $x\in P$ に対して $F_x=\mathbb Q(x)$ とし、$n_x$ を $x$ の $\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式の次数とするので、$n_x\ge1$ である。$x$ は $F_x$ の指定された生成元としても扱う。$h_x=\log H_{1,F_x}(x)/n_x$ と定める。ここで $\log H_{1,F_x}$ は数体の高さの構成による対数的高さである。また、$D_x=\log|\operatorname{disc}(F_x)|/n_x$、$R_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\log N\mathfrak p_v$ と定める。この和は $v(x)\ne1$ または $v(x-1)\ne1$ を満たす $F_x$ の有限素点を走り、$N\mathfrak p_v$ は対応する極大イデアルの絶対ノルムを表す。$J_x=256(x^2-x+1)^3/(x^2(x-1)^2)$、$A_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_v\max\{\log(v(J_x)),0\}$ とする。後者の和は $F_x$ のすべての有限素点を走り、非零の項が有限個の場合にはそれらの和を取り、そうでなければ零とする規約による。$J_x$ の分母は零ではないが、$J_x$ 自身は零となり得る。使用する実対数では $\log0=0$ であるため、その場合には後者の和の各項は零である。データ $K=(V,c)$ は、自然数の有限集合 $V$、その各元が素数であることの証明、$2\in V$ の証明、および任意の実数 $c$ からなる。$S_K\subseteq P$ は、剰余体の標数が $V$ に属する各有限素点 $v$ について $|\log(v(x))|\le c$ と $|\log(v(x-1))|\le c$ がともに成り立ち、$F_x$ の各無限素点 $w$ についても $|\log(w(x))|\le c$ と $|\log(w(x-1))|\le c$ がともに成り立つ点の集合である。各素点の値は与えられた数体の構成による。$c$ の符号に制限はなく、$S_K$ は空でもよい。$\Delta_d=552960d$、$e(\delta,t)=(60\delta)^2\log(2\delta t)/\sqrt t$ と書き、実対数、平方根、除法には全域で定義された演算を用いる。 次の三つの命題を仮定する。第一に、任意のデータ $K$ に対して実数 $B$ が存在し、すべての $x\in S_K$ が $|A_x/6-h_x|\le B$ を満たす。第二に、任意の正の自然数 $d$ と任意のデータ $K$ に対して、有限集合 $E\subseteq P$ と実数 $H_2,C_2$ が存在し、$n_x\le d$、$x\notin E$、$H_2\le A_x$ を満たすすべての $x\in S_K$ が $A_x/6\le(1+e(\Delta_d,A_x))(D_x+R_x)+C_2$、$e(\Delta_d,A_x)\le1$、$0\le D_x+R_x$ を同時に満たす。第三に、任意の三つの実数 $\delta,t,\eta$ について、$1\le\delta$、$0<\eta$、$(((60\delta)^2(2\delta+4))/\eta)^4\le t$、$1\le t$ ならば $e(\delta,t)\le\eta$ である。これら三つの仮定のもとで、任意の正の自然数 $d$、任意の正の実数 $\varepsilon$、任意のデータ $K$ に対して実数 $H,C$ が存在し、$x\in S_K$、$n_x\le d$、狭義不等式 $H<h_x$ を満たすすべての $x\in P$ が $h_x\le(1+\varepsilon)(D_x+R_x)+C$ を満たす。存在量化された実定数には、いずれも符号の制限を課さない。第二の仮定の有限例外集合は空でもよく、$S_K$ や指定した次数範囲に含まれる必要もない。結論には例外集合を設けない。これらの仮定と結論は $d=0$ では要求を課さず、条件を満たす点の集合が空ならば対応する各点についての要求は空虚に成立する。
source: Shinichi Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, §2, Corollary 2.2(i)–(iii) and proof of Corollary 2.3; https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Inter-universal%20Teichmuller%20Theory%20IV.pdf . Independently adapted under Apache 2.0; no Iut or Genl imports. Exact source composition refer/iut/Iut/Implication/Corollary23.lean:56–112. The three Open children imply HighHeightEstimate by absorbing the finite exceptional set below a height threshold, transferring between the two fixed heights and applying the explicit error bound. This conditional combination does not close any of its three children.
